Personally, I think the Rand tackles human nature and to what extent the pursuit of happiness is intertwined with it. I think she handled this very well. As voluminous as the book is, I never found myself gasping for air. I found Rand's writing style one which constantly refreshed my mind, rid it of fatigue. I think Rand crafted her ideal world, which any fiction writer reaches for.

That said, I think Ayn Rand herself was a parasitic leech. The antithesis of what she held upon a pedestal. She fed upon controversy and the false attention brought with it. A cornerstone right of her philosophy, objectivism, is liberty. Yet, she believed objectivism was the only correct way of thinking. This is quite the contradiction and by no means free.

I don't like objectivism as an argument for liberty. I'm all for rational self interest but not the metaphysical approach which I don't think naturally leads to it as a conclusion.
